messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa**, water freezes at approximately **–2 °C** (about 271.15 K).  

This is slightly below the standard freezing point of 0 °C at 1 atm (101.3 kPa). The decrease in freezing point with reduced pressure is due to the phase diagram of water, where the triple point occurs at 6.112 kPa and 273.16 K.
